name: How do I choose between a single-hole and a widespread faucet?

mainEntity.name: How do I choose between a single-hole and a widespread faucet?

acceptedAnswer.text: Before purchasing a new fixture, check the number of mounting holes in your sink or countertop, the hole spacing (such as 4-inch or 8-inch spread), and the clearance under overhead cabinets. Single-hole faucets offer a clean look, while widespread faucets spread handles and spouts across multiple holes. If you choose a single-hole faucet for a pre-drilled three-hole sink, you will need an escutcheon deck plate to conceal the unused holes. Confirming these dimensions ensures the new fixture fits your cabinetry and backsplash seamlessly.
acceptedAnswer.description: Check your sink or countertop hole pattern: single-hole faucets fit compact spaces or use deck plates, while widespread faucets need three separate holes set 8 inches apart.
